correctness.rationale: For distributional BV modulo constants, integrate unit-step residuals against Df; the upper bound by the best single step is attained at the level of the supremum. Integral preservation follows from the Bernstein basis integrals 1/(n+1), so the error of a jump at s equals twice the integral of its sampled response on (0,s). On cell j with u=(n+1)s−j the response is the Bernstein tail above j plus (1−u)p_{n,j}. Differentiating the basis-integral binomial tail gives (n+1) integral_0^s p_{n,j}=sum_{k>j}p_{n,k}(s)+s p_{n,j}(s). This reduces the error derivative to 2p_{n,j}(s)[j+1−(n+2)s]. As a separate check of the exact peak heights, this derivative is that of 2s(1−s)p_{n,j}(s). These primitives match at cell boundaries because successive Bernstein masses coincide there, and they vanish at 0, so this is the entire cell profile. Thus each cell's strict peak lies at (j+1)/(n+2), and every interior cell boundary is a strict minimum. At its peak the height is proportional to a_j a_(n−j), a_k=(k+1)^(k+1)/k!. The ratio a_(k+1)/a_k strictly decreases because d[(t+1)log(1+1/t)]/dt=log(1+1/t)−1/t<0. This gives the precise central parity maxima and the formulas by substitution, also C_0=1/2. Every norming derivative measure is concentrated on winning jumps; both odd-degree jumps together lead to opposite residual signs on (a,b) for coefficients of the same sign or on (0,a) for coefficients of opposite signs, so only a single nonzero jump can attain equality. Stirling at j=n/2+O(1), s=1/2+O(1/n) gives the claimed 1/sqrt(2 pi) limit. The uploaded verification notes and checker were read, not executed. Their finite tests are not used to certify all degrees or all BV inputs.
